blockers: pointer: backwards (R3) -- signed pointer offset count[len]
interface_change: none
notes: One-token rewrite: count[len] -> count[static_cast<std::size_t>(len)]. Sound only because len >= 8 on every caller path (caller BuildJpegHuffmanTable passes len in 9..16) -- the cast moves a precondition (len non-negative) from the type into an unchecked assumption; the driver cannot exercise len<0 since the original is UB there. This is a mechanical rewrite a normalizer could do IF it can prove the index non-negative; an LLM did it here by reading the caller. static const -> const at namespace scope (FR-264 accepts either). 400 trials x len 8..16 incl. negative counts.

Every caller (all blocked, all take State*) must be rewritten to pass state->data, state->pos.

The certification therefore covers the function, not the call-site rewrite every caller would need -- that is where the trust problem moves.

notes: FOUND HAZARD (aliasing -> copy). The original enqueues a NON-OWNING chunk that aliases jpg.tail_data; the subset has no way to store a borrow inside a container element, so the rewrite copies. Natural driver (enqueue, then read the queue): byte-identical on all 5 legs -> CERTIFIED. Adversarial driver (mutate tail_data after enqueue, then read): the original shows the mutated bytes, the rewrite the old ones -> r_san/r_rs/r_back DIFF on 50/50 lines. The byte-diff catches it ONLY if the driver author thinks to mutate after enqueue; a driver that just calls the function and prints the result certifies a semantic change. In brunsli the tail is not mutated after EncodeEOI, so the rewrite is probably correct in context -- but that is a whole-program fact the per-function certificate does not establish. Harness STUBS JPEGData/SerializationState to the touched fields.

The original data=nullptr makes any write after Finish UB; the rewrite panics on such a write (buf empty) -- not driven. 60 trials, 0-3 rounds, chunk sizes 0..11 and the full 16384, double Finish (no-op path). Certified chunk contents (len+hash) and writer fields.

Copy-vs-borrow of the input is unobservable here but costs an O(n) copy per resume (Resume is called per input chunk in streaming decode).
